If one account encounters a transient rate limit or secondary checkpoint returning HTTP 403, unbuffered error handlers frequently mark the account as permanently disabled and immediately divert traffic to adjacent accounts. This triggers a rapid domino effect, falsely disabling the entire account pool within minutes even though the accounts remain active and healthy upstream.
